steps.title: Sterilize surgical tools and microprism
steps.instruction: Place the 30° diamond knife, 45° microprism (1.5 mm, silver‑coated), forceps, scissors and other surgical tools in a UV‑C LED sanitizer box for the recommended time; do NOT autoclave the diamond knife or microprism because high temperature can break the blade and deform the prism.

steps.title: Prepare anesthesia and analgesia solutions
steps.instruction: Make the following injectable solutions: • Ketamine stock: dilute 1 mL of 100 mg mL⁻¹ Ketamine Hydrochloride to 10 mg mL⁻¹ with saline (dose 100 mg kg⁻¹). • Rompun stock: dilute 0.15 mL of 20 mg mL⁻¹ Xylazine to 0.3 mg mL⁻¹ (dose 3 mg kg⁻¹). • Acepromazine stock: dilute 0.15 mL of 10 mg mL⁻¹ to 0.15 mg mL⁻¹ (dose 1.5 mg kg⁻¹). • Add 8.7 mL sterile 0.9 % NaCl to reach the final injection volume. • Carprofen: 0.5 mg mL⁻¹ in sterile saline (dose 5 mg kg⁻¹). • Dexamethasone: 2 mg mL⁻¹ solution, give 5 mg kg⁻¹ (effective concentration 0.5 mg mL⁻¹). • Lidocaine 2 % in sterile saline for local analgesia.

steps.title: Anesthetize and secure the mouse
steps.instruction: Inject the mouse intraperitoneally with the ketamine/xylazine/acepromazine mixture at the calculated doses (100 mg kg⁻¹ ketamine, 3 mg kg⁻¹ xylazine, 1.5 mg kg⁻¹ acepromazine). Administer dexamethasone (5 mg kg⁻¹) and carprofen (5 mg kg⁻¹) subcutaneously. Apply lidocaine 2 % locally if needed. Place the animal in a stereotaxic frame, maintain body temperature with a heating pad that has a feedback thermometer, and keep the head level.

steps.title: Create cranial window over the inferior colliculus
steps.instruction: Under a microscope at high magnification, drill a circular craniotomy over the IC using a size #80 micro‑drill bit while delivering a continuous stream of cold air and cold 0.9 % saline onto the skull. Monitor the bone thickness to avoid puncturing the soft tissue beneath; stop drilling as soon as the thin bone layer is reached.

steps.title: Remove dura mater gently
steps.instruction: Using fine scissors or Dumont #5 forceps, carefully tear and lift the dura mater only over the IC region, avoiding the midline veins and sinuses. Keep the exposed brain surface continuously moist with sterile saline to prevent drying.

steps.title: Clean and prepare the diamond knife
steps.instruction: Inspect the 30° diamond knife for a smooth, clean surface; if any debris is present, rinse with sterile saline and dry with a sterile cotton tip. Sterilize the knife by UV exposure (do not autoclave).

steps.title: Create tissue pocket with diamond knife
steps.instruction: Insert the sterilized diamond knife into the soft tissue adjacent to the IC to form a shallow pocket. Retract the knife by 0.3–0.5 mm before withdrawing completely so that the pocket remains open for microprism insertion.

steps.title: Insert the 45° microprism
steps.instruction: Using fine forceps, place the 45° microprism (1.5 mm, silver‑coated) into the sulcus between the IC and the cerebellum such that the orthogonal side of the prism faces the lateral surface of the IC. Ensure the prism sits flush without excessive force; avoid repeated insertion attempts. Keep the IC surface wet with sterile saline throughout.

steps.title: Seal the window with cover glass and agarose
steps.instruction: Place a 5 mm #1 cover glass over the implanted prism. Prepare low‑melting agarose at 1–2 % (maximum 2 %) by heating to 33–37 °C, then cool to a liquid but not hot state. Apply a thin layer of agarose over the cover glass to immobilize the prism and maintain optical clarity. Allow the agarose to solidify before proceeding.

steps.title: Set up two‑photon imaging system
steps.instruction: Mount the mouse under the two‑photon microscope (Insight X3 laser, 1040 nm for jRGECO1a). Install the 16× water‑immersion objective (NA 0.8, WD 3.0 mm) or 4× air objective as needed. Connect the Hamamatsu H7422PA‑4 PMT, t565lp dichroic, and the following emission filters: et525/70 m for GFP and et595/50 m for jRGECO1a. Load Prairie View (v5.8) and verify laser power and shutter status.

steps.title: Adjust calcium signal intensity
steps.instruction: During initial imaging, observe basal calcium fluorescence. If signals are too dim, gently advance the microprism to improve contact; if signals are overly bright, retract slightly to avoid tissue damage. Aim for intermediate intensity indicating proper prism‑tissue coupling without excessive injury.

steps.title: Record calcium responses to pure tones
steps.instruction: Present a series of pure‑tone stimuli (varying frequency and amplitude) while continuously acquiring two‑photon movies of GFP and jRGECO1a signals. Ensure the laser remains on, the shutter is open, and the appropriate filters are in place. Save raw movies for later analysis.

steps.title: Lesion field of view for histological verification
steps.instruction: After functional imaging, increase laser power to a high‑power setting and raster the beam over the entire field of view to create a permanent lesion. This marks the imaged region for subsequent histology.

steps.title: Fix and process brain tissue
steps.instruction: Perfuse the mouse with 4 % PFA in PBS, then extract the brain and post‑fix in 4 % PFA for at least 24 h. Transfer the tissue to 30 % sucrose in PBS until it sinks. Embed in OCT compound, freeze, and cut coronal sections on a cryostat. Mount sections on slides, cover with Vectashield mounting medium containing DAPI, and image the lesion site to confirm microprism location.

steps.title: Analyze imaging data
steps.instruction: Load the recorded movies on a computer equipped with Windows, Python, ImageJ, Origin Pro, and Adobe Photoshop. Draw regions of interest (ROIs) around individual neurons, extract fluorescence traces, and compute tone‑evoked calcium responses. Perform statistical analysis as described in the manuscript.
